For STL, 3MF, OBJ and STEP the “Material” box shows the volume, weight and length of 1.75 mm filament of what is exported. It counts like the file: visible bodies only, holes taken off, overlaps only once. On the right you pick the filament - PLA, PETG, ABS, ASA, TPU or PA (nylon) - and the weight follows its density. The volume is the body's own. Weight and filament are a rough estimate for a print with walls and infill: you set the “Preenchimento” (15 % to begin with) and the “Paredes” (2) under the heading, and the box says what it counted and what the same part would weigh solid. Your slicer's own settings decide the real number, so take it as a guide: good for comparing designs and for whether the spool will last. At 100 % infill the box counts the part as solid, the upper bound. The box works out its numbers when you press “Calcular”, so the export window opens at once even for a finely traced model.

Importing

With “Importar” or Ctrl+I you bring foreign files into the design.

  • “Abrir projeto do layerling”: A layerling design (.lyl, or an older .skf) comes back as a new design.
  • “Inserir neste projeto”: The bodies of a layerling design are added to the open one. Handy for basic shapes you need again and again: build them once, save them and bring them in every time. Drop one or more .lyl files on the drop zone below and they are inserted the same way. Its notes come along, closed and numbered on after the ones already in the design, and so do its reference points.
  • “Insert from the server”: The same for a design kept on the server (shown when there is a server store). Pick the folder and click the design; its bodies are added to the open one.
  • DXF: A DXF, as a laser cutting shop or a supplier sends a part outline, comes in as parts to work on: every closed outline a body 4 mm high and every hole in it a hole of its own beside it (a round one a cylinder), so a hole is moved and sized in the 3D editor like any other; select them all to move the part. In millimetres (a file in inches is converted, one without a unit is read as millimetres), arcs and circles kept as true arcs. Lines, arcs, circles, ellipses, polylines, splines and blocks are read; text, dimensions and hatches are left out, and outlines that do not close too - the message says how many. Set the thickness in the properties.
  • Add geometry: Drop STL, OBJ, 3MF, STEP, SVG, PNG or JPG files in the window or click to choose a file. Imported meshes can be turned, moved, cut with holes and built upon. A STEP file with several solids, an assembly from another CAD program, comes in as one body each under the name the file gives it, in its place to the others and in the colour the file gives it; several bodies under one entry of the file, the screws of a part say, become a part each. Its assemblies become bundles under their names, an assembly inside one a bundle inside the bundle; so a whole assembly hides or moves at once, and a double click opens it to work on a single part. An SVG comes in as a sketch body, one from a tracer such as picsvg.com or Inkscape's "Trace Bitmap" as well: its outlines become the lines and curves of a sketch, 4 mm high and reading from above as in the drawing. In the properties you set its “Preenchimento”, an area or a stroke outside, inside or centred, and “Silhueta (sem furos)” leaves the holes out, see Sketches, "Fill and silhouette". You change the points themselves in sketch mode. If it should come in at a size of your own, type the width in the import window under SVG and picture: width in mm first, as in Tinkercad: the drawing is scaled to it, height and depth with it, and the field is empty again after that one import; left empty, an SVG comes in at its own size and a picture 50 mm wide. Only a very intricate SVG with more than 2500 lines and curves comes in as a fixed mesh. A PNG or JPG picture is traced into an outline and comes in the same way, as a sketch body 50 mm wide that you can resize afterwards: the part of the picture that is not its background, the background being the part that takes up more of the picture's edge. An SVG that holds nothing but one picture is traced the same way. A shape that cannot be built into a solid, such as an outline that crosses itself or touches itself at a point, is left out, and after the import layerling says how many there were. Then it helps to join overlapping pieces in the drawing program, close the outlines and save the file again. Drawings made on one page, such as the layers of one document exported as separate files, line up again when you switch on “SVG: manter o lugar na página do desenho” in the import window before you import them: each keeps its place on the page, where otherwise each is centred on itself. An SVG drawn in several colours comes in as one body per colour as well, each in its colour and in its place; with more than 12 colours, as a traced picture has, it stays one body. A coloured OBJ or 3MF comes in as one body per colour, each in its place. In an OBJ the colours sit either in the file itself, as in an OBJ from layerling, or in an .mtl beside it. Select that one too, or import the whole ZIP the way Tinkercad hands out its OBJ. A 3MF carries its colours itself, and in a project from Bambu Studio, OrcaSlicer or PrusaSlicer each part takes the colour of its filament. A 3MF with several objects, such as a project with one object per plate, comes in as one body per object; modifiers, negative volumes and support blockers from the slicer are left out. Colour painted onto faces in the slicer is not read.
  • From Tinkercad: An STL or OBJ export from Tinkercad comes in as geometry like any other mesh, and an OBJ keeps the colours. The real shapes come across with a free tool from the community: Export to layerling by taylormadearmy, a bookmark that converts a Tinkercad design in your browser into a .lyl file, which you open here with “Abrir projeto do layerling”. It is not part of layerling and we have not tested it ourselves yet; its author tested it on Windows with Chrome.

A design saved with a newer layerling may hold things your version does not know yet, such as a new shape, a new setting or fonts of one's own. If layerling cannot open it for that reason, the message names both versions. If it opens, the notice says that newer things may look different here. Either way, reloading the page helps: layerling.com always serves the newest version. The installed app picks it up the next time it starts; on your own server you install the update.

Template pictures are added in sketch mode, see Sketches.

Simplifying an imported mesh

A scanned or sculpted mesh often has far more triangles than its shape needs, and every one of them is carried along while you move, cut and save. “Simplificar malha” in the Modify group (or in the right-click menu of the body) shows the mesh as it is next to what a chosen share of its triangles would leave of it; both views turn and zoom together with the mouse buttons of the workplane. Set how much to keep as a percentage or a number of triangles, and “Simplificar” takes the lighter mesh. The result is a plain mesh: for the result of a cut or merge, “Editar grupo” and its original parts are given up. With “Keep edges and holes” switched on, as it is to begin with, sharp edges and the rims of holes stay exactly where they are while flat faces still lose most of their triangles; switched off, the simplifier may round them off to reach a lower count. If the simplifier stops above the number you asked for, the window says so and why: with “Keep edges and holes” on, a body made of flat faces and sharp edges, such as boxes and wedges, often cannot lose more.

Cutting, merging and intersecting an imported mesh is calculated in your browser, so the workspace settings limit how many triangles such a mesh may have (“Cortar malhas importadas de até”). A mesh above the limit is not processed, and the message names its triangle count; simplify the mesh first, or raise the limit if your computer can take it.

Making an imported mesh exact

An STL, OBJ or 3MF file holds only triangles, even when the part was drawn in CAD with flat faces and round bores. “Make exact” in the “Modificar” group (or in the right-click menu of the body) looks through those triangles for the planes, cylinders, cones, spheres and tori they were made of and rebuilds the body from them as an exact CAD body: a bore becomes one real cylinder with a round rim instead of a hundred narrow strips. After that, “Arredondamento” and “Chanfro” follow one clean edge, “Excluir face” takes away a whole rounding or the wall of a hole, and a STEP export carries the real faces. The status line says what was found, such as "planes: 9, cylinders: 4".

What fits none of these surfaces stays as small flat facets, and the message says how much of the surface that is. A body that is mostly free-form, such as a figure or a sculpted shape, stays a mesh, and so does a mesh with gaps or crossed walls, which cannot close into a solid. Up to 400,000 triangles are taken, and a large mesh can take a few minutes. A larger mesh goes below that with “Simplificar malha” and “Keep edges and holes” switched on; otherwise take the mesh as it came, it comes out cleanest. One undo step brings the mesh back.

For a small mesh with round faces, up to 4,000 triangles, the edge tools do this by themselves: rounding an edge of such an STL rebuilds it the same way first.

Reporting a bug

If layerling does something unexpected, save a “Relatar erro”: the link sits in the footer at the bottom, next to the forum. It is a ZIP file, because GitHub and many forums refuse a bare .lyl: inside are your design as a .lyl and a short text file with the version, browser, screen size, the last messages and any errors. The start page opens the ZIP like a backup, or you unpack it and open the .lyl. Nothing personal is in it. Attach the file to your post in the forum or on GitHub, so the problem can be followed with exactly your design.

If layerling stops with an error, a window with the error message shows instead of a blank page. From it you can save the state of the design last stored in the browser as a .lyl file, go back to the overview, or start a new design. The error message from the window and the saved file help when you report it.

Shared designs on a server

When layerling runs on your own computer or web server, it can offer a shared folder in which all users keep designs. The start page then holds the designs in two tabs, “Servidor” for the shared folder and one for this browser, each with the number of designs in it; the one with more designs comes first and is open. You create folders there, move designs by dragging and search across the whole folder. A design that lives there saves itself back to it. A design from this browser goes onto the server by dragging its card onto the “Servidor” tab, or with “Enviar para o servidor” in the card's menu. While the “Servidor” tab is open, “Criar novo projeto 3D” and “Restaurar backup” put the design into the server folder you have open, and “Fazer backup de tudo” packs every design of the server, in its folders, and its custom shapes into one ZIP file. The start page shows a design by its file name, so renaming a design, on its card or at the top of the editor, renames the file on the server too. Deleting a design or a folder removes it for good, together with its working copy in this browser. Custom shapes kept on the server sit in its folder Custom shapes, see Shapes.

Two things make that quicker: “Enviar tudo para o servidor” on the start page puts every design of this browser on the server in one go, and ticking “Novos projetos no servidor” makes every new design start in the server folder, so it is saved there from the first change on. With the tick, everything else that makes a design starts there too: opening or importing a file, “Restaurar backup” (with the backup's folders), duplicating and taking a state from the history, each into the server folder you had open; “Nova pasta” on the start page then makes a folder on the server. A design made in the first moments waits until the server has answered. When new designs must always start on the server and this browser holds none of its own, the start page shows only the server's designs. The tick is kept in this browser. A design that cannot go - its name is taken on the server, say - stays in the browser, and the message says how many.

The other export formats (STL, 3MF, OBJ, STEP, SVG, PNG and the drawing) can go into the same folder: in the export window, “Salvar no servidor” writes the file next to your design, or into the folder you have open on the start page for a design that is not on the server. A program that shares the folder, such as a slicer in Docker, can open it from there. The file does not appear in the list of designs. If a file of that name is already there, the message says so, and pressing the button again replaces it.

That is not simultaneous editing: whoever opens a file works on a copy of their own. If somebody else has changed the file in the meantime, layerling refuses to overwrite it.

On layerling.com this function is not switched on. How to set it up on your own server is described in the README on GitHub.

13. Atalhos de teclado

Todas as teclas num só lugar, tiradas direto do programa, então a lista está sempre certa.

Os atalhos funcionam enquanto o plano de trabalho estiver em foco. Enquanto você digita num campo, eles não atrapalham. No Mac, Cmd vale sempre que aqui aparece Ctrl.

No editor, “Atalhos de teclado” na área “Ajuda” abre a mesma lista numa janela. O botão de impressora na janela (“Imprimir ou salvar como PDF”) imprime só a lista, em preto sobre branco, a lista inteira em um lado de uma folha A4 ou Carta, em três colunas, para deixar à mão como referência rápida. Na janela de impressão do navegador, você também pode salvar como PDF.

A caixa no alto da janela pesquisa a lista: ela mantém só os atalhos cuja frase, grupo ou teclas contêm todas as palavras digitadas, então "arredondamento" ou "ctrl+z" deixa só essas linhas. Maiúsculas e acentos não importam, e uma única letra ou dígito encontra essa tecla e as palavras que começam com ela. O X no fim da caixa a esvazia; com a caixa vazia, a lista inteira volta. O botão de impressora imprime o que a janela mostra, então depois de uma pesquisa imprime só os atalhos encontrados.

Pesquisa de comandos

Não acha uma ferramenta? Pressione Ctrl+K ou clique na lupa na área “Ajuda” e digite o que você procura: uma ferramenta ("arredondamento", "espelhar"), uma forma ("cilindro") ou um comando ("exportar", "desfazer"). Navegue com as setas e pressione Enter, ou clique na entrada.

  • A pesquisa entende a palavra em português, em inglês e em alemão, e ignora maiúsculas e acentos: "aushoehlen" encontra “Vazar”.
  • Cada entrada mostra o atalho de teclado e o grupo da barra de opções em que ela fica. Assim, você aprende onde encontrá-la.
  • Entradas em cinza não podem ser executadas agora, na maioria das vezes porque nada está selecionado. Elas continuam na lista para que a pesquisa ainda mostre onde a ferramenta fica.

O guia que você está lendo também tem uma caixa de pesquisa, no topo de cada página: digite uma ou duas palavras e ela lista as seções que contêm todas elas, com as palavras encontradas destacadas. Clique numa delas, ou pressione Enter para a primeira, para ir direto até lá. A página que se abre destaca cada lugar onde suas palavras aparecem e rola até o primeiro naquela seção; Esc ou um clique num destaque os remove.

  • O nome de uma forma adiciona essa forma ao plano de trabalho, como clicar nela no menu de formas.
  • Com o campo vazio, a pesquisa de comandos lista no topo os comandos que você usou por último.
  • O nome de um sólido do seu projeto encontra esse sólido e o seleciona, o que ajuda num projeto com muitas peças. Os sólidos só aparecem depois que você digita.
  • Uma forma personalizada que você salvou também é encontrada pelo nome assim que você digita, e um clique a insere no projeto como no painel de formas.
  • A pesquisa de comandos também funciona no modo de esboço, com as ferramentas de esboço.

Suas próprias teclas

Qualquer comando da pesquisa de comandos pode ir para uma tecla sua: uma ferramenta que você usa o tempo todo, uma forma, “Centralizar no plano de trabalho” ou “Abrir o painel de formas”.

  1. Abra “Atalhos de teclado” e clique em “Adicionar uma tecla” sob “Suas próprias teclas”, no alto da janela.
  2. Digite algumas letras do comando e clique nele, ou pressione Enter para o primeiro.
  3. Pressione a tecla que quiser, sozinha ou com Ctrl, Alt ou Shift. Letras, números e F1 a F12 podem receber um comando.

Uma tecla que o editor já usa, uma que o navegador guarda para si (como Ctrl+W) ou uma das suas próprias teclas é recusada, e a janela diz para que ela serve. Clique numa tecla da lista para trocá-la, no X ao lado para removê-la, ou em “Remover todas as minhas teclas” para recomeçar.

  • A tecla executa o comando exatamente como a pesquisa de comandos. Se agora ele não puder ser executado, quase sempre porque nada está selecionado, a barra de status avisa.
  • Suas teclas aparecem ao lado dos comandos na pesquisa de comandos e na lista impressa.
  • Elas ficam neste navegador, como o tema. Uma tecla para uma ferramenta de esboço funciona no modo de esboço, uma para o editor 3D fora dele.
  • Enquanto você digita num campo, suas teclas ficam de lado, como todas as outras.

Ajuda interativa

Não acha onde ler sobre um botão ou um campo? Deixe o programa levar você até lá. Clique no ponto de interrogação na área “Ajuda”, ou pressione Shift+F1. O ponteiro vira um ponto de interrogação, e o que estiver embaixo dele fica contornado.

  • Clique num botão, num campo, numa chave, numa alça, numa área da barra de opções ou na barra de título de uma janela. O elemento não faz o que normalmente faz. Em vez disso, abre uma pequena janela com o nome do elemento, um resumo curto da parte deste guia que fala dele, até dois outros lugares que o mencionam e o botão “Abrir no guia”.
  • A ajuda é sobre o elemento que você apontou, não sobre a janela inteira em volta dele. Um elemento sem nome próprio usa o mais próximo em volta dele; dentro de uma janela, ele recorre ao ponto de interrogação dessa janela.
  • “Abrir no guia” abre o guia nessa seção numa nova aba. Na nova aba, a seção fica com um contorno colorido, do título até o fim, para você ver onde ela começa e termina.
  • Se o guia não fala nada sobre o elemento, a janela diz isso e oferece “Pesquisar no guia”.
  • Esc, ou o ponto de interrogação de novo, sai do modo. Numa tela sensível ao toque não existe passar o mouse por cima: um toque num elemento abre a janela na hora.

A janela se move pela barra de título, como as outras janelas. O programa encontra a seção pelo nome do elemento (o texto de um botão, o nome de um campo), porque este guia usa os nomes dos botões exatamente como aparecem no programa. Ele procura na mesma pesquisa da caixa no topo de cada página do guia, no idioma que você está usando, e roda inteiramente no seu navegador.

14. Building with an AI (MCP)

How an AI assistant such as Gemini, Claude or Codex creates and changes shapes, groups them and takes pictures of the view in your open editor.

Este capítulo ainda não foi traduzido para o português. Segue o texto em inglês.

layerling comes with an MCP server. MCP is a standard through which an AI assistant can use tools in other programs. With it an AI client such as Gemini, Claude or Codex sees an open editor tab and works in it: it creates shapes, changes dimensions, groups, cuts, rounds edges, reads out the scene and takes pictures of the view. You describe the part, the AI builds it, you watch and can step in at any moment.

The bridge between AI client and editor runs locally on your computer. Keep in mind, though: what the AI reads, meaning the scene and the pictures of the view, goes to the provider of your AI client, like any other input there.

Important: The MCP bridge exists in the development server that you start yourself on your computer. On layerling.com and in installations with static hosting it is switched off. A copy you host yourself, such as the Docker image on a NAS, can switch it on with an access token; see "A copy on a NAS or server" below.

Step by step for beginners

You do not need to know anything about programming for this.

The shortest way: give your favourite AI the address of the project, https://github.com/henmedia/layerling, and ask it: "Set up layerling on my computer so that I can build 3D models with you through its MCP server." It downloads and installs everything itself and tells you when it is done. This works with an AI that can work on your computer, such as the Code tab of the Claude app, Codex, Antigravity or Gemini CLI. A chat in the browser cannot do it, because it cannot install anything on your computer.

Or do it yourself, on Windows with the Claude app, in five steps:

1. Install layerling. Open the Start menu, type PowerShell and open Windows PowerShell. Copy this line, paste it into the window with a right-click and press Enter:

irm https://raw.githubusercontent.com/henmedia/layerling/main/scripts/windows-quickstart.ps1 | iex

It installs what layerling needs, downloads layerling into the folder layerling in your user folder (C:\Users\<your name>\layerling) and opens it in your browser. The first time this takes a few minutes.

2. Keep layerling running. layerling runs as long as the PowerShell window stays open, and the AI can only build while it runs. Next time, double-click "Start layerling" on your desktop instead.

3. Install the Claude app. Install the Claude app for Windows and sign in. The Code tab used in the next step is part of the paid Claude plans.

4. Open the layerling folder in the Code tab. In the Claude app, switch to Code at the top and choose the folder layerling in your user folder as the folder to work in. layerling already brings everything Claude needs to find its tools. If Claude asks whether it may use the MCP server "layerling" of this folder, allow it.

5. Tell Claude what to build. For example: "Use the layerling tools and build me a round box, 60 mm across and 40 mm high, with a 2.5 mm wall." If no editor is open, Claude opens one in your browser, builds the box there step by step and takes pictures to check its work. You watch and can change anything yourself at any time.

On a Mac it goes the same way, with these changes. In step 1, open the Terminal app (press Cmd+Space, type Terminal and press Enter), paste this line and press Enter:

curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/henmedia/layerling/main/scripts/mac-quickstart.sh | sh

If Git or Node.js is missing, it tells you what to install (macOS offers Git in a window, Node.js comes as an installer from nodejs.org); afterwards run the same line again. In step 2, the shortcut on your desktop is also called "Start layerling". In step 3, install the Claude app for Mac.

Tip: If something does not work, tell Claude what you see. It can read the error and usually fixes it itself. If nothing happens in the editor, check first that layerling is still running (step 2).

Setting up

  1. Get layerling from GitHub and start it in the project folder with npm run dev. Node.js must be installed. On Windows the quick-start line in the README takes care of that.
  2. Open an editor tab, for example http://127.0.0.1:3000/?editor=1. You can leave that to the AI: when no editor is open, the first tool that needs one starts your browser with an editor and waits until it has connected. That works for a layerling on your own computer; a copy on a NAS or server needs you to open the editor. Set LAYERLING_MCP_OPEN_EDITOR=0 for the MCP server to switch it off.
  3. Connect your AI client to the MCP server. The client starts it itself with node scripts/layerling-mcp-server.mjs.

Claude Code

Nothing to install: the project brings a .mcp.json that registers the server, and the skill under .claude/skills/layerling-mcp-skill. Open the layerling folder in Claude Code and ask, for example: "Use the layerling MCP tools to list my open editors and inspect the scene."

Claude Desktop

Claude Desktop does not read project files. Enter the server in its own configuration. As a template use docs/mcp/claude-desktop-config.example.json in the project, replacing the script path with the absolute path on your computer. Then restart Claude Desktop.

Codex

Copy the skill from docs/skills/layerling-mcp-skill into your Codex skills folder, enter the server in your Codex configuration using docs/mcp/codex-config.example.toml, and restart Codex.

Gemini & Antigravity

Antigravity auto-discovers the workspace skill in .agents/skills/layerling-mcp-skill. For Gemini CLI, copy the skill from docs/skills/layerling-mcp-skill into your global skills folder (~/.gemini/skills/), add the server to your settings using docs/mcp/gemini-config.example.json, and restart the client.

The detailed instructions for each client are in the README on GitHub.

A copy on a NAS or server

A copy you host yourself can let an AI client drive its open editors over the network. It is off by default, because whoever can drive the bridge can read and change the open designs. On the server, set LAYERLING_MCP_REMOTE to true and LAYERLING_MCP_TOKEN to a secret of at least 16 characters (for the Docker image in environment: of the compose file; no rebuild needed). Open an editor tab of that copy and keep it open, and give the MCP client the address and the same token: LAYERLING_URL=http://nas:3000 and LAYERLING_MCP_TOKEN=<the token>.

Only a client with the token can list or drive the editors. The editor pages need none, but they only count under an address or name that only your own network can use (an IP address, a name without a dot, or one ending in .local or .lan); a real domain behind a reverse proxy goes into LAYERLING_MCP_ALLOWED_HOSTS. Use it on a network you trust, and HTTPS beyond it. The README has the details.

What the AI can do

The AI works with the same functions as you, through the same path as your operation in the editor. New layerling functions get their MCP action right away. The tools:

ToolWhat it does
layerling_list_editorslists the open editor tabs
layerling_rename_projectgives the project a name, as the pencil beside the project name does
layerling_open_editoropens a new editor tab in your default browser and waits until it has connected (on your own computer only)
layerling_read_scenereads scene, selection, units and the exact dimensions of all objects
layerling_list_objectslists all objects with dimensions, position, rotation and id
layerling_select_objectsselects objects
layerling_hide_othershides everything but the selection or the given objects, in one undo step
layerling_delete_objectsdeletes objects
layerling_move_objectmoves an object to another place in the object list
layerling_create_shapecreates a shape: box, cylinder, text (also curved), thread, gear, sketch body and all the others
layerling_import_fileimports a file as the import window does, a coloured OBJ or 3MF as one body per colour, a 3MF with several objects as one body per object
layerling_add_fontadds a font of one's own for text from a TrueType, OpenType or WOFF file; it stays in the browser, a design keeps only the letters it uses
layerling_list_fontslists the built-in fonts and the fonts of one's own, with id and name
layerling_import_meshbrings a triangle mesh into the design
layerling_update_objectchanges dimensions, position, colour, name, solid or hole and everything else that makes up the shape, a text's letter edge included
layerling_align_objectsaligns objects with each other
layerling_scale_objectsscales objects by a percentage, together or each in place
layerling_lay_flatlays an object with one face on the plate
layerling_place_on_facesets objects down on a face of another, sloped ones too, like the C key
layerling_perforate_facecuts a hole pattern into a flat face or round the wall of a cylinder, tube or bore; the holes stay as holes grouped with the body
layerling_sweep_sketchpulls a rectangular or round cross-section along a path of points as one exact body; a closed path makes a ring
layerling_push_facepushes a flat face out or cuts a pocket into it, with an inset from the edge and a corner radius; the new part is a sketch body grouped with the body, or a free body of its own with separate
layerling_paintpaints parts of a body in colours of their own for printing in several colours (Paint): fill a face up to its sharp edges, a round patch, or a lasso drawn in a flat view; erase, clear; saved with the body and written to a 3MF as painted faces
layerling_support_ribstands a thin support rib under the lower face of a part printed tilted on one edge, with bridges one layer high (Support rib)
layerling_stencil_bridgesholds the parts of a plate with text cut through that would fall out, with bridges grouped with the plate, as wide and high as set (Stencil bridges)
layerling_mate_facesbrings a face of one object against a face of another, face to face or flush, or puts two round faces on one axis
layerling_open_groupopens a group so its parts can be changed one by one, also a group inside an open one
layerling_close_groupcloses it again ("Done") or cancels
layerling_add_to_groupputs loose objects into a group without opening it
layerling_take_out_of_grouptakes one part out of a group without opening it
layerling_group_objectsgroups objects
layerling_ungroup_objectsdissolves groups
layerling_boolean_cutcuts solids with holes
layerling_intersect_objectskeeps only what the objects have in common (Intersection)
layerling_hull_objectswraps the objects in one convex body, as if shrink-wrapped (Hull)
layerling_cookie_cuttermakes a cookie cutter from the objects: a wall with a cutting edge and a rim round the mirrored outline (Cookie cutter)
layerling_flexi_jointscuts a flat body into links with joints printed in place that swing to the sides (Flexi joints)
layerling_make_lidmakes a lid for a body open at the top: pushed in, over the top or flat, with the fit you choose and magnets if you like (Lid)
layerling_make_cable_channelruns a round channel for a cable through a body from an entry to an exit, finding the way itself with gentle bends (Cable channel)
layerling_loft_sketchesjoins two sketch bodies into a loft from one outline to the other (Loft sketches)
layerling_separate_partsseparates a shape into its loose parts, a sketch body into one body per outline
layerling_split_objectscuts solids or holes in two with a plane
layerling_list_edgeslists the real CAD edges of an object
layerling_apply_edge_treatmentchamfers or fillets chosen edges
layerling_hollow_objecthollows a body with an even wall
layerling_cut_outcuts one solid out of another so they fit: the part stays, a copy grown by the clearance is subtracted from the other body
layerling_punchpunches the outline of one solid, seen along x, y or z, straight through another; the punch stays and need not touch it
layerling_offset_objectbuilds the clearance of a press fit: grows or shrinks a solid, or adds the grown copy as a hole, or moves only the sides
layerling_list_faceslists the faces of an exact body
layerling_delete_facesdeletes faces and closes the gap
layerling_array_objectsmultiplies in a row, in a grid or on a circle
layerling_bundle_objectsbundles objects like Ctrl+B: they move together, keep their colour and kind and go out separately in an export
layerling_layer_textturns a text into a stack of layers for a multicolour print (letters, wider rims, a plate without holes) or builds a stack again, with a key ring hole, the corners per layer and a rounded or chamfered letter edge; with a name list, one tag per name
layerling_text_blockmakes a text block: a text becomes the first of several lines, each a text of its own under the one above, aligned left, centred or right, each line the same size or smaller
layerling_layer_iconturns an SVG icon (the text of the file, or an extruded sketch body) into a layered icon tag for a multicolour print - the icon, wider rims, a plate without holes - or builds one again with a new width or layers; with a count it fills the plate with copies
layerling_create_qr_codemakes a QR code from a text or web address, like “QR code” in the shape library - the code alone, raised on a plate or engraved, with error correction, width, height, quiet zone and as a hole if asked; it warns when a module gets under 0.8 mm
layerling_create_sbc_boardplaces an SBC board true to size, like “Placa SBC” in the shape library - Raspberry Pi 5, 4, 3 B+, Zero 2 W or BIGTREETECH Pi, with its holes and connectors, the clearance round the edge connectors, the position and as a hole to cut a case
layerling_reference_imageadds a reference image from a picture, as “Imagem de referência” does, or moves, turns, calibrates (two points of the picture and their real distance), fades or locks one - a guide that is never exported or printed; trace turns its dark or light part into a sketch body standing on it
layerling_measure_sectionmeasures on a cutting plane between two points that snap to the outline - wall thickness, gaps, fits
layerling_show_overhangsswitches the overhang hatching on or off, sets the angle and reports for each body the area that would need supports
layerling_estimate_printestimates volume, weight and filament for the selection or the whole design: for a solid body, and as a rough guess with walls and infill like the export window
layerling_check_clearancechecks before printing which parts overlap, touch or come closer than a minimum gap (Check clearance), the separate parts of one object too
layerling_printer_playreads, sets or clears the printer's play (“Printer play” in the settings) and places the fit test that measures it
layerling_check_printchecks before printing what would go wrong: walls too thin for the nozzle, floating parts, small contact with the plate, overhangs and open meshes (Print check)
layerling_add_reference_pointsmarks reference points - on the centre, corners or edge middles of objects, or at exact positions - that shapes snap to
layerling_list_reference_pointslists the reference points with their ids and positions
layerling_remove_reference_pointsdeletes reference points by id, or all of them
layerling_list_notesreads the user's notes with their text, the body each is pinned to and whether it is a request for the AI
layerling_wait_for_noteswaits until you tick “For the AI” on a note, and hands the request over at once
layerling_add_noteputs a note on the model, pinned to an object or free on the plate
layerling_update_notechanges a note or answers it; an answer closes the request
layerling_remove_notesdeletes notes by id
layerling_inspect_errorsshows the last message and the last error, plus the messages and errors of the session
layerling_wrap_around_cylinderwraps a body lying flat, an SVG or text for example, around a cylinder, outward or inward as an engraving
layerling_texture_surfacelays a surface texture onto a body: grooves, knurling, honeycomb or bumps, for grip or for looks, and changes or removes it later
layerling_simplify_meshreduces the triangle count of an imported mesh, to a share in percent or to a number of triangles
layerling_make_exactturns an imported mesh into an exact CAD body: planes, cylinders, cones, spheres and tori become real faces, so edges round cleanly and STEP carries them
layerling_save_custom_shapekeeps bodies as a custom shape, on the server or in the browser, to insert them into other designs
layerling_list_custom_shapeslists the custom shapes on the server and in the browser
layerling_insert_custom_shapeinserts a custom shape into the open design, at a spot x/z if you like
layerling_delete_custom_shaperemoves a custom shape; inserted bodies stay
layerling_show_workplanehides and shows the plate with its grid, for a picture of the underside for example (only the view)
layerling_set_section_viewcuts the view open along a plane to look inside (only the view, nothing is cut apart)
layerling_measurementsshows or hides the measurements of the tape measure and lists them with their lengths, hides or shows the sizes around the selection like Q, and types a length for one of them, which moves the body at its end like a click on its number
layerling_measure_anglemeasures an angle like the protractor: at the corner of three points or between two flat faces, and shows it in the view
layerling_saved_viewsaves the current view under the key 7, 8, 9 or 0 and goes back to it, like Shift+key and the key (only the view); also sets the start view of new designs
layerling_build_plateslists, adds, names, orders and removes the build plates, moves objects onto a plate and arranges them on the plates, like the plate bar
layerling_clear_historydeletes every undo step for good, as the History view's "Delete history" button does; needs confirm: true
layerling_set_history_viewlooks back at an earlier state of the project, like the History view (the real design stays untouched; changing tools wait until it is closed)
layerling_restore_from_historybrings objects (also parts inside groups) back from an earlier state into the design as copies, as the History view's Bring into design does - one step that undo takes back
layerling_export_section_svgreturns the outlines on a cutting plane as an SVG at 1:1, from the same bodies as the export
layerling_sketch_from_sectionmakes a sketch from the outlines on a cutting plane, lying on the cut: opened in the editor to change, or built at once into a body of a given height
layerling_export_drawingmakes the workshop drawing of the "2D" export: three views at 1:1 on an ISO sheet with overall sizes and a table of the round bores, as SVG text or PDF
layerling_export_meshwrites the file of the export window as STL, 3MF, OBJ, SVG (top view, footprint or visible edges) or DXF for laser cutting, from the same bodies; to a path on this computer, or as base64
layerling_save_projectsaves the whole editable design as a .lyl file at a path on the computer where the MCP server runs, without a dialog; an existing file is only replaced with overwrite, it is written through a temporary file, and the target of Ctrl+S in the editor stays as it is
layerling_list_attachmentslists the files attached to the design (name, type, size), as the Attachments panel shows them
layerling_get_attachmentreads one attached file, its bytes as base64, as Download in the panel does
layerling_add_attachmentattaches a file given as base64, with the panel's checks; a name already attached is only overwritten with replace
layerling_rename_attachmentgives an attached file another name; its content stays
layerling_remove_attachmentremoves an attached file for good; needs confirm: true
layerling_set_workplaneputs the workplane on a side of a body or back on the base plate, and hides or shows it
layerling_capture_imagetakes a picture of the view: front, top, side, diagonally from a corner and more

That lets the AI check itself: it creates something, takes a picture, looks and improves.

An example

You say: "Build me a round box 60 mm across, 40 mm high with a 2.5 mm wall, open at the top, plus a flat lid with 'Tea' written in an arc." The AI creates the cylinders, hollows one, puts the curved text on the lid and takes pictures at the end to see whether it fits.

Tip: Give the AI concrete dimensions and tell it what the part is for ("holder for a 12 mm rod, fits a Bambu Lab A1"). Then it makes more sensible decisions. And watch it build: you can step in yourself at any time, because it is the same editor.

15. Instalação como app, uso offline e hospedagem própria

Como abrir o layerling como um programa comum, mesmo sem rede, e como rodá-lo no seu próprio computador.

Instalando como app

layerling pode ser instalado como um programa comum. Ele ganha então um ícone e uma janela próprios, sem barra de endereços. Depois da primeira visita, ele abre mesmo sem internet. Seus projetos continuam no seu computador. Vale a pena instalar: o app abre mais rápido (porque não precisa ser carregado de novo toda vez), funciona sem internet e alivia o servidor. Você não perde nada, já que o layerling continua avisando quando sai uma versão nova. Isso também protege os seus projetos: o Safari no Mac, no iPhone e no iPad apaga os dados guardados de um site que não é visitado há sete dias, mas não os de um app instalado.

Se o seu navegador permitir, aparece na página inicial uma dica com “Instalar agora”. Caso contrário:

  • Chrome e Edge: clique no ícone de instalação à direita da barra de endereços, ou escolha "Instalar como app" no menu do navegador.
  • Safari no Mac: menu "Arquivo", depois "Adicionar ao Dock".
  • Safari no iPhone e no iPad: ícone de compartilhar, depois "Adicionar à Tela de Início".
  • Firefox: não instala apps. Mesmo assim, o layerling abre offline numa aba.

Você pode fechar a dica na página inicial com “Ocultar esta dica”. No Chrome ou no Edge, abrir o app instalado uma segunda vez traz a janela já aberta para a frente, em vez de abrir outra.

No computador, o layerling instalado no Chrome ou no Edge também se registra como programa para arquivos .lyl: no gerenciador de arquivos, um clique duplo num projeto abre o projeto no layerling, e Ctrl+S salva de volta nesse arquivo. O app instalado também se registra para abrir arquivos .stl e .3mf. Cada arquivo abre como um projeto novo, assim como quando você usa “Abrir um projeto ou importar geometria” na página inicial. Para abrir esses arquivos sempre com o layerling, escolha-o em "Abrir com" e defina-o como programa padrão. No Android isso não funciona, porque lá o navegador não associa arquivos a web apps instalados; abra o projeto com “Abrir um projeto ou importar geometria” na página inicial.

Atualizações

Quando existe uma versão mais nova, o layerling mostra isso na página inicial. Em “Notas da versão e download” você lê o que mudou. O número da versão fica no canto inferior direito. Depois de recarregar a página, você está na versão nova.

No layerling.com e em outros servidores web, uma página aberta percebe sozinha que há uma atualização. De tempos em tempos, sempre que você volta para a aba e logo que a página não encontra um arquivo do programa de que precisa, ela pergunta ao servidor qual é a versão. Se algo novo foi instalado nesse meio-tempo, um cartão no canto inferior direito avisa e lista as novidades. “Salvar e recarregar” primeiro grava no navegador o projeto que está aberto e depois carrega a página de novo; o projeto volta do jeito que você deixou. “Depois” adia o cartão por 15 minutos. Recarregue logo: uma página que fica na versão antiga pode carregar partes da nova que não combinam com ela.

O mesmo cartão aparece quando isso já aconteceu: os módulos de cálculo de CAD, que só carregam quando você precisa deles pela primeira vez, informam de qual versão são. Se não for a da própria página (depois de uma atualização, ou com uma cópia guardada de uma versão antiga), o cartão pede que você recarregue antes que os dois deixem de se entender.

Quando o layerling está aberto em várias abas, elas cuidam umas das outras: se outra aba já roda uma versão mais nova, na parte de baixo da aba antiga, um aviso pede que você a recarregue. E se o mesmo projeto estiver aberto em duas abas, as duas avisam, porque salvam automaticamente e uma sobrescreveria a outra. Se você abrir o layerling em mais uma aba enquanto já há uma aberta, a nova aba sugere continuar na antiga e se oferece para fechar. Se você quiser duas abas de propósito, por exemplo para dois projetos lado a lado, clique em “Continuar trabalhando aqui” na nova aba. Este guia também abre numa aba própria: enquanto o layerling estiver aberto ao lado, o botão do guia, no canto superior direito, diz "Voltar ao editor" e fecha o guia, em vez de abrir o editor uma segunda vez.

Idioma e aparência

Você escolhe o idioma no canto superior direito, na lista de idiomas. O esquema de cores ao lado oferece “Sistema” (segue o sistema operacional), “Claro”, “Escuro” e “Grafite”, um cinza-escuro neutro.

Rodando por conta própria

layerling é software livre (AGPL-3.0) e pode rodar no seu próprio computador ou servidor, por exemplo numa oficina, num clube ou numa escola. Há várias formas, descritas no README no GitHub:

  • O início rápido no Windows: uma única linha no PowerShell instala tudo e põe um atalho na área de trabalho. Se o layerling já estiver rodando, outro clique duplo não inicia um segundo servidor, só abre a página.
  • Docker: para NAS (dispositivos de armazenamento em rede) e servidores domésticos, sem precisar instalar o Node.js. Cada versão sai como uma imagem pronta henmedia/layerling no Docker Hub (também ghcr.io/henmedia/layerling) para amd64 e arm64; docker run -d -p 3000:3000 -v layerling-thumbnails:/app/.codex/project-thumbnails henmedia/layerling:latest inicia o layerling, e num NAS você procura a imagem no registro do gerenciador de contêineres. O volume layerling-thumbnails mantém as miniaturas da página inicial quando você atualiza; sem ele, elas somem toda vez que o contêiner é criado de novo, até você abrir o projeto.
  • Exportação estática: o resultado são arquivos simples que qualquer servidor web consegue servir. Eles precisam ficar na raiz de um endereço (https://layerling.example.com/ ou http://192.168.0.5:8080/), não numa subpasta nem abertos direto do disco; o README traz o passo a passo. Se o servidor tiver PHP e houver uma pasta store gravável ao lado do index.html, a exportação também passa a ser o armazenamento compartilhado de projetos.

A ponte MCP para assistentes de IA só existe no servidor de desenvolvimento; veja Construindo com uma IA.

Ajuda e feedback

  • No editor, a área “Ajuda” tem o “Guia rápido”, com as principais ações, e a visão geral dos atalhos de teclado. Cada seção do guia rápido tem um ponto de interrogação que leva ao capítulo correspondente deste guia.
  • Perguntas, sugestões e relatos de bugs são bem-vindos no fórum e no GitHub.
  • O que mudou em cada versão está nas notas da versão, que você encontra no rodapé da página inicial e do editor.

Vídeos que outras pessoas fizeram sobre o layerling.

Feitos por outras pessoas

Estes vídeos não são deste projeto. Os links abrem o YouTube numa nova aba; nada é carregado do YouTube até você clicar.

  • Layerling Tutorials – HL ModTech (inglês). Uma playlist de alguém que usa o Tinkercad, por enquanto com uma apresentação de cerca de 23 minutos do layerling (CAD gratuito no navegador que vai além do Tinkercad), uma análise mais detalhada dos recursos e uma rápida atualização sobre roscas impressas.
  • Layerling – Playlist – Making Layers (inglês). Uma série sobre o layerling, por enquanto com "Tinkercad alternative / upgrade? Introducing Layerling!" (uma visão geral para quem vem do Tinkercad) e "Layerling Sketch Tools!" (sobre as ferramentas de esboço).
  • Layerling – TECHNOBENTO (inglês). Uma playlist sobre o layerling, por enquanto com “A new way to sketch in Layerling”.
  • Layerling CAD Videos – Printology (inglês). Uma playlist sobre o layerling, por enquanto com “I'm 100% In on Layerling - The Next Big Free CAD” e “Layerling Features That Blow Tinkercad Out Of The Water”.
  • I Tried Layerling After Tinkercad… Is It REALLY Better? – Maker Mates Studio 3D Printing (inglês). Alguém que vem do Tinkercad experimenta o layerling e compara os dois.
  • Print by Layer – Print N Repeat (inglês). Uma playlist sobre o layerling, por enquanto com “The EASIEST Way to Design Hinges in Layerling” e “The EASIEST Way to 3D Model Threads!”.
  • Tinkercad Too Basic? Fusion 360 Too Much? Meet Layerling for 3D Printing – 3D Jesus | 3D Printing & Design (inglês). Um primeiro teste do layerling sem nenhum manual: arredondamentos e chanfros, sólidos ocos, roscas, esboços, sólidos de revolução, padrões, importação e perfis de impressora.
  • Layerling en español | Del primer contacto al proyecto completo – Random Maker (espanhol). Uma playlist em espanhol, do primeiro contato com o layerling até projetos completos: no que ele difere do Tinkercad, a comparação ponto a ponto e como levar projetos de um para o outro.
  • Proyectos en Layerling – Fulcro 1900 (espanhol). Uma playlist de projetos no layerling, por enquanto com uma apresentação do layerling como ferramenta gratuita mais completa que o Tinkercad, acessórios de mesa (três modelos), uma capa de celular e uma barra roscada, porca e parafuso.
  • Layerling – Werkplaats Marc (holandês). Uma playlist sobre o layerling, por enquanto com uma apresentação inicial para quem usa o Tinkercad (“Layerling - De Gratis Tussenstap van Tinkercad naar Fusion 360”) e um tutorial sobre esboços: desenho por cima de uma foto, revolução e varredura ao longo de um caminho (“Schetsen Uitgelegd”).

17. Tablet and touch

Working with fingers or a stylus: selecting several bodies, turning and zooming the view, the long press menu, and what to know on an iPad.

Este capítulo ainda não foi traduzido para o português. Segue o texto em inglês.

Fingers and a stylus

layerling runs in the browser of a tablet, and as an app from its home screen. A finger does what the left mouse button does. Three things a tablet does not have, a right mouse button, a Shift key and a wheel, have a way of their own:

You want toOn a tablet
Select a bodyTap it.
Select several bodiesTap a body: a round button appears in the lower left. Tap it, and every further body you tap joins the selection; a tap on a selected body takes it out again. A tap on empty space changes nothing; a second tap on the button ends it and clears the selection. Or hold a finger still for half a second, choose “Selecionar vários”, then tap one body after another.
Select all bodiesHold a finger still on empty space for half a second, choose “Selecionar tudo”.
Open the menu of a right clickHold a finger still on a body or on empty space for half a second.
Move a bodyDrag it.
Resize, turn or lift a bodyDrag its handles, the small squares and arrows around it. A finger catches them from a little beside.
Turn the viewOne finger on empty space, or drag the view cube.
Zoom the viewTwo fingers: spread to come closer, pinch to go away.
Move the viewSlide two fingers together.
Clear the selectionTap empty space. Not while “Girar a vista com um dedo” is on, where one finger turns the view; and in “Selecionar vários” the first tap on empty space only ends the mode and leaves the selection as it is, the next one clears it.

Selecting several bodies

Without a Shift key, “Selecionar vários” in the menu of a long press does what Shift+click does on a computer. While it is on, a message says so, and each tap on a body adds it to the selection or takes it out again. A tap on empty space, or Esc on a keyboard, ends it and leaves the selection as it is. A finger on empty space still turns the view meanwhile. Then “Grupo de união”, “Alinhar” or a move work on all the bodies you picked.

The same menu has “Colocar sobre uma face”, the key C for a touch screen. The selection then follows the finger over the faces of other bodies; a tap sets it down on the face you tap, even a sloped one, and the first tap is enough. The menu entry is also found by searching for "set down" or "cruise" (the command search, Ctrl+K on a keyboard).

Turning and zooming the view

One finger on empty space turns the view, two fingers zoom and move it. A finger that starts on a body works on the body, not on the view. If you would rather have it turn the view, switch on “Girar a vista com um dedo” in the view bar: one finger then turns the view instead of selecting, wherever it starts. That switch only shows on a device with a touch screen.

The view cube in the top left turns the view when you drag it, and a tap on one of its sides, corners or edges jumps to that view. See View and workplane.

Handles, small points and a stylus

A fingertip covers what it aims at. layerling lets a finger reach a little further to handles, points, lines and edges than a mouse pointer does, but a stylus is finer. This holds for a pen the tablet knows as a pen, such as an Apple Pencil or an S Pen. A plain stylus with a rubber tip counts as a finger for the screen and is not finer than one, so work with it as with a finger. An Apple Pencil that hovers above the screen on an iPad also shows the name of a control after a moment, in a small bubble, as the mouse pointer does with a tooltip.

In sketch mode, “Freehand” draws with the pen or a finger as on paper; when you lift it, the line becomes sketch points you can edit, see Sketches.

If bodies slip when children or hurried hands touch them, switch on “Selecionar antes de mover” in the settings: a body then has to be selected first, and only the next drag moves it.

On an iPad or iPhone

  • Install it as an app. In Safari, tap the Share icon and choose "Add to Home Screen". The app opens in a window of its own without the address bar, and it works without a connection, see Offline and install.
  • Your designs live in the browser (unless you host layerling yourself and set up a server folder). There is no account, and nothing is uploaded. Safari has a rule of its own against tracking: it deletes what a website stored after seven days in which you did not visit it in Safari. A web app added to the Home Screen is exempt from that rule, as WebKit documents it. That is one more reason to use the app from the Home Screen, and to back up important work: “Fazer backup de tudo” on the start page packs all designs into one file.
  • Files. Safari lets a page write into a file only through a download, so “Exportar” puts the file into the Downloads of the Files app, and Ctrl+S on a keyboard downloads it again; see Files and saving.
  • No keyboard needed. Every tool has a button in the ribbon, and a number field opens the on-screen keyboard. A keyboard on the iPad adds the keyboard shortcuts. A value box beside a body opens its number field with the second tap: the first tap only marks it, so a finger that lands on it by accident does not raise the keyboard.

Workshops with children

Fingers and rubber-tip styluses work alike here. Two settings make a class easier: “Selecionar antes de mover” so that a touch does not move a body by accident, and “Girar a vista com um dedo” so that one finger always turns the view. The question mark button in the Help group of the ribbon switches on the “Ajuda interativa”: a tap on any button, field or handle then explains it, and the same button, or Esc, leaves it.

For a whole class, switch on “Modo simplificado” in the settings. The ribbon then keeps only the tools a workshop uses (copy, paste, duplicate, delete, undo, group, mirror, chamfer, fillet, hollow, align, export), the shape library a short list, the buttons are larger, and the start page shows the designs and nothing else: no news, no welcome text, no help buttons and no links out of layerling. Switching it on is a tap; switching it off is a press held for two seconds on the button that then takes its place. A link ending in ?mode=simple switches it on for the device that opens it, ?mode=full switches it off again. Whoever runs layerling on a server can start everyone in it with LAYERLING_SIMPLE_MODE=true, or fix it for everyone with always, so that the program has no switch to leave it; see the README.

Este guia cresce junto com o programa. Se algo estiver faltando ou errado, avise nas discussões.
